text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To help narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever or visible blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) secondary to a sexually transmitted infection (likely Chlamydia or Gonorrhea).

The patient's history of dyspareunia, inconsistent condom use, and lower abdominal pain suggests an ascending infection. I will confirm this with a specific test. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture; REQUEST TEST: NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea. REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound.
